claims.claim: Consideration is commonly described in introductory U.S. law as a mutual exchange of promises or obligations, rather than a gratuitous promise.
Consideration can involve money, property, a promise, or a right; money is not required for the introductory exchange concept.
California Civil Code section 1605 frames consideration in terms of a benefit to the promisor or prejudice to the promisee used as an inducement, while excluding a burden already legally owed.
A completed act performed before a later promise can raise a past-consideration issue because the act was not necessarily requested as the later promise's exchange.
At a high level, performing only a duty already owed can raise a preexisting-duty consideration issue when another party later promises additional payment without receiving new performance.
Whether a particular contract or modification is enforceable depends on governing law, transaction type, facts, and possible jurisdictional rules or exceptions.
